title: Pizza with meat and stuffed crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with meat (excluding pepperoni) and a stuffed crust is a classic Italian dish where a thin dough base is topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and a variety of meats such as ham, chicken, beef, or sausage. The stuffed crust contains an inner layer of cheese, making it especially flavorful and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Neapolitan pizza is baked in a wood‑fired oven at about 485 °C for 60–90 seconds.
Stuffed crust was introduced in the United States in the 1990s as a way to add extra cheesy goodness.
Meat toppings often include smoked ham, chicken breast, or ground beef, but never pepperoni in this variation.
There are more than 30 dough styles for pizza, ranging from thin “Neapolitan” to thicker “Chicago” style.
In Italy, pizza is often served with minimal toppings to let the dough and sauce shine.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella cheese supplies calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain crust deliver vitamins B6 and B12, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The combination of carbs, fats, and protein provides lasting satiety and energy.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Meat‑topped pizza with a cheese‑filled crust can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and meat contain saturated fats, which can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meats often contain a lot of salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should choose alternative cheeses.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pizza hot, sliced into individual portions. Fresh herbs (basil, oregano) or a light green salad make a nice accompaniment. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain dough and reduce the amount of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crispy.
